text:
morgan: anyone seeing tiny-gpu pods stuck pending in ap-southeast-2a warmpool? ~30 of them, scheduler keeps skipping nodes :grimacing:
lee: hmm, which class of pods? 0.125/0.25 gpu ones?
shreya: probably fractional-gang stuff again, those request sizes fragment racks fast
diego: can you grab `kubectl get pods -n ai -o wide | grep Pending` and `kubectl get nodes -l warmpool=ap-southeast-2a --show-labels`?
morgan: quick paste:
```
NAME                       READY   STATUS    NODE             NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
trainer-small-58c9        0/1     Pending   <none>           <none>           <none>
...
```
chun: autoscaler-bot posted earlier: "taint added: gpu-reserve=high:NoSchedule on 5 nodes in ap-southeast-2a"
autoscaler-bot: [alert] added taint gpu-reserve=high for capacity smoothing (rule: short-burst-protect)
lee: ah that explains it — taint plus strict nodeAffinity on these pods will cause skip chain. are these pods tolerating that taint?
morgan: they do not. operator added nodeAffinity `key: rack` so pods prefer same-rack for data locality, but the reserve taint landed on the only compatible racks
shreya: so we have soft fragmentation: racks with tiny free slots got pinned by reserve taints, leaving pods that need locality but no tolerations
diego: two levers: relax affinity (not great for perf) or add toleration+preferNoSchedule to the pods + canary rollout, or change autoscaler to respect fractional packing weight (reduce taint footprint)
chun: also seeing increased inter-node egress on those racks — network overlay flapped yesterday and autoscaler pre-provisioned nodes in a different AZ, then re-tainted back to original racks which confused placement
lee: can we try patching one deployment with toleration and `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` for the affinity? quick test to see if scheduler can place them without moving data
morgan: patching one now, will post status in 2m
(2 minutes later)
morgan: patched, 6 pods moved to Running on nodes with toleration applied :thumbsup:
shreya: good signal. we should avoid mass relax — maybe add a small admission controller that adds a toleration for short-lived pods in warmpool if autoscaler-taint exists
diego: long term we should change warmpool policy: reserve taint only on nodes with >= X contiguous tiny slots free, otherwise we create islanding and fragmentation
chun: also moving some of the warmpool capacity to a compact pool (larger slots) at night could reduce fragmentation cost; right now tiny slots sit idle and cost >0.12 GPU-hour each when reserved
lee: +1 on compact pool experiment. schedule a canary and monitor evictions/latency. add a metric for "tiny-slot-utilization" in console
morgan: filing quick RFC for two changes: (1) autoscaler taint policy tweak, (2) admission hook for short-lived tiny pods toleration. tagging @shreya @diego for review
shreya: ack, will prioritize. also run a one-off descheduler job to coalesce tiny pods where possible to free contiguous slots
diego: note: descheduler may trigger evictions — plan a rate limit and eviction budget so we don't cascade spikes
chun: logging note — capture `scheduler_events` traces for these placement skips; will help tune weight heuristics
morgan: thanks all — rolling plan: patch toleration canary (done), open RFC for autoscaler change, run descheduler with budget, and schedule compact-pool canary overnight. will update thread with links
lee: awesome. :eyes: keep an eye on cost dashboard while we compact, mutable savings may appear within 24h
shreya: postmortem-esque note: this was an interaction between reserve taints + strict affinity + transient network AZ drift. triple threat :thinking_face:
morgan: yep. labeling this thread `infra:frag` and `action:autoscaler-rfc`
